dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Primary lateral sclerosis

The combination of generalized hyperreflexia, exaggerated jaw reflex with abnormal head/neck responses (a pseudobulbar sign indicating bilateral corticobulbar tract involvement), and the absence of weakness, atrophy, or lower motor neuron signs — in the setting of a completely normal MRI brain and unremarkable blood work — points to a pure upper motor neuron neurodegenerative process.

Alternatives:
1. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (early, predominantly upper motor neuron presentation before lower motor neuron signs emerge)
2. Hereditary spastic paraplegia
3. Neurosyphilis (general paresis)
order_raw:
